summary: Describes mesh-enhanced SLP, which adds to the Service Location Protocol a set of Directory Agents that peer with each other in shared scopes and swap new service registrations. This improves reliability and scalability of finding services on a network. It is an experimental specification.

eli5.summary: A town may have several help desks that list local services. This memo has the help desks share their lists, so asking any desk gets a good answer even if one goes away.

questions: service location protocol directory agent peering
how do directory agents share services
is mslp backward compatible with slp
subtitle: Directory agents in a service discovery network share registrations with each other.

tldr.problem: In Service Location Protocol (SLP), when multiple Directory Agents serve the same network scope, they do not automatically share information. Service agents must register with each Directory Agent independently, creating redundant registrations and management complexity.
tldr.mechanism: Mesh-enhanced SLP (mSLP) adds a fully-meshed peering architecture where all Directory Agents serving a scope establish peer connections and automatically propagate service registrations to each other. Registrations are shared using anti-entropy (periodic reconciliation) and direct forwarding mechanisms, ensuring consistency across all agents.
tldr.outcome: Service agents only need to register with one or a few Directory Agents; the registrations automatically propagate to others. The system becomes more reliable and simpler to manage. mSLP remains experimental and is backward compatible with standard SLP.

facts.label: Connection type
facts.value: Persistent TCP connection per peer pair

today: mSLP remains an experimental protocol and has not advanced to standards track. Standard SLP (RFC 2608) continues as the primary service discovery mechanism, though mSLP provides an approach for improving reliability in multi-agent deployments. The design principles of mSLP, particularly the fully-meshed peering model, have influenced later service discovery and consensus protocols.

sections.title: The Service Discovery Challenge
sections.content: Service Location Protocol (SLP) allows computers and services to advertise their presence on a network, making it easy for applications to discover what services are available. In larger deployments, Directory Agents (DAs) are used to improve performance and scalability. A single Directory Agent can serve multiple network scopes, and a single scope can be served by multiple DAs. However, the original SLP specification does not define how multiple DAs serving the same scope should interact. This creates a problem: a Service Agent (SA) must discover and register with every Directory Agent serving its scopes, creating redundant registrations and complex management. mSLP solves this by having Directory Agents form a fully-meshed peer network that automatically shares registrations.
sections.eli5: When you list your business with multiple directories, you have to keep calling each one to update your information. With mSLP, you only call one, and it automatically tells the others.

sections.title: The Mesh-Enhanced Architecture
sections.content: mSLP introduces the concept of Mesh-enhanced DAs (MDAs) that form a fully-meshed peering relationship. For each network scope, all MDAs serving that scope establish direct peer connections to every other MDA serving the same scope, creating a complete mesh topology. A single persistent TCP connection between each pair of peers carries all service registrations for the scopes they share. Mesh-enhanced SAs (MSAs) can now register with just one or a subset of MDAs whose scopes cover their needs, and their registrations automatically propagate through the mesh to reach all other MDAs. This architecture provides several benefits: newly booted MDAs can catch up on all new registrations from their peers without requiring re-registration from Service Agents, the consistency of service data across all DAs is automatically maintained, and the number of connections and registration messages is reduced compared to traditional SLP.
sections.eli5: Instead of being separate help desks, they become one network where each desk tells the others about new services. A service only registers once, and everyone finds out about it automatically.

sections.title: How Registrations Spread
sections.content: mSLP uses two mechanisms to distribute service registrations across the mesh: direct forwarding and anti-entropy. When a Service Agent sends a registration with the Mesh Forwarding extension to an MDA, that MDA forwards the registration to all its peers. Each registration is tagged with an accept ID (the MDA that first accepted it and a timestamp) and a version timestamp (assigned by the Service Agent). These timestamps ensure that registrations are applied in the correct order and that newer versions always overwrite older ones, even when they arrive out of order due to network delays. Anti-entropy is a background reconciliation mechanism: each MDA periodically queries its peers for registrations it may have missed, ensuring consistency even after network failures. mSLP also tracks a summary vector for each peer relationship, recording the latest registration from each accept DA, which allows MDAs to quickly identify gaps in their knowledge and request only missing registrations.
sections.eli5: When you register a service with one help desk, it tells all the others right away (direct forwarding). If a message gets lost, the desks periodically ask each other about missing services (anti-entropy), so everything stays up to date.

sections.title: Backward Compatibility and Scaling
sections.content: mSLP is designed as a lightweight enhancement to SLP and maintains full backward compatibility. Mesh-enhanced entities (MDAs and MSAs) work as ordinary DAs and SAs when interacting with non-enhanced entities, allowing gradual deployment. An enhanced MDA can coexist with ordinary DAs in the same network, providing mesh benefits where MDAs are deployed while remaining interoperable with legacy devices. The full-mesh topology, while simple and reliable for small to medium deployments, does not scale to very large numbers of MDAs in a single mesh. The specification recommends that mSLP work best when the number of MDAs in a mesh is on the order of tens or below. For larger deployments, administrators can split a scope into multiple finer scopes, each with its own mesh, creating a hierarchical structure that scales better while maintaining the benefits of automatic registration propagation.
sections.eli5: mSLP works alongside regular SLP, so you can mix old and new help desks. It works great for a reasonable number of desks, but if you have too many, you split them into groups.
